description: I am participating individually in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. I am a Computer Engineering student interested in AI, technology, innovation, and problem-solving. I look forward to exploring new ideas and developing a creative solution to a real-world challenge.
summary:
I developed VitalGuard, a web-based astronaut health monitoring and decision-support prototype for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

The project uses real NASA OSDR OSD-575 blood-serum biomarker data from the SpaceX Inspiration4 mission. It compares each crew member's later biomarker measurements with their own pre-flight baseline to identify unusual changes.

The website includes an interactive dashboard, biomarker trends, a 300-feature heatmap, explainable alerts, crew comparisons and a method and safety section.

My goal is to make complex health measurements easier to understand and help identify changes that may need human medical review.

The current prototype analyses stored pre-flight and post-flight serum measurements. Live wearable monitoring is a proposed future extension, not a feature currently connected to the website.
details:
About VitalGuard

VitalGuard is a React-based web application developed to explore personalised astronaut health monitoring using NASA biomarker data.

How my website works

1. Home Dashboard – Displays the selected crew member, sample information and biomarker shift index.

2. Biomarkers – Displays biomarker trends and a heatmap covering 300 analytes.

3. Alerts – Identifies measurements that move outside the crew member's personal baseline and explains the changes.

4. Crew Overview – Allows comparison of the four coded Inspiration4 crew members.

5. Method and Safety – Explains the calculation method, missing data and limitations.

My analysis method

The first three pre-flight samples are used to establish an individual baseline range for each biomarker. Later measurements are compared with that range.

A marker is flagged when it goes at least one complete baseline range-width beyond the personal range.

The shift index is calculated as:

Shift Index = (Flagged analytes / Analytes with valid measurements) x 100.

For example, C001 at R+82 displays a 30% shift index, representing 89 out of 300 measured analytes.

Technology used

React, JavaScript, CSS, Vite, React Router and GitHub Pages.

Future scope

I propose integrating heart rate, ECG, oxygen saturation, temperature, scheduled blood pressure and movement sensors through a wearable system fitted beneath an astronaut's suit.

These are future hardware and software integrations, not live readings in the current prototype.

Limitations

The present website is a research and decision-support prototype. Its alerts are based on explainable rules and are not a trained diagnostic AI or clinically validated medical system. Human review is essential.
